useCase.name: Let a guardian ask to meet a teacher about their own child, and have the teacher offer a slot from their own free time

intent.summary: A guardian asks to meet a teacher who teaches their own child. One step, and the teacher chooses the time.

request.gloss: let the teacher propose the time themselves

routesElsewhere.note: The teacher chooses the slot, not the guardian. The guardian may state a preference and the teacher meets it where they can (BR-3).

request.text: parent-teacher meeting mein milenge
request.gloss: we will meet at the parent-teacher meeting

routesElsewhere.note: That is the school-wide meeting day, and it carries no slot at all: families attend during the announced window and see the teachers who are present (UC-14-11 BR-10). This is the everyday case, and it does carry a slot — the teacher chooses it (BR-9).

request.text: ustad ne bulaya hai
request.gloss: the teacher has asked to meet

routesElsewhere.note: Where the teacher raised it, the slot is proposed first and the guardian confirms (UC-14-12 BR-4).

steps.note: One step. No coordinator is required for any of this to proceed — requiring one would make an everyday conversation into an event (BR-8), and there is no window, no slot grid and no opening or closing date (BR-9).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A teacher who does not teach the child is not offered, and a child who is not the guardian's is refused.
plan.atomicity: One write: the request and the audit entry together or not at all. **No time is fixed.** The teacher reads the reason, is offered the slots in which they are genuinely free, and chooses one (BR-2, BR-3). A request is never deleted — a declined or cancelled one stays on the record, so a family who asked three times and was declined three times is visible (BR-11).

operations.name: meeting.request.submit
operations.idempotencyKey: guardian_id + student_id + teacher_id + reason, since the same ask twice is one request
operations.purpose: Record a guardian's request to meet a teacher about their own child.

parameters.name: guardian_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the teachers who teach the child, with their subject.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: 20 to 500 characters, written by the guardian (E3). What the teacher reads before deciding, so it is the family's own words.

parameters.name: timing_preference

parameters.name: branch_id

errors.meaning: The teacher does not teach that child.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. It is what the teacher reads before deciding whether and when to meet (BR-2), and a reason a planner wrote is a family's concern described by somebody who does not have it.
Never propose or fix a time. The teacher chooses the slot, not the guardian — that is what distinguishes this from the scheduled event (BR-3), and a preference stated is not a booking made.
Never request a teacher who does not teach the child. They are not offered at all (BR-1, E1), and asking would put a family in front of somebody with nothing to say about their child.
Report earlier requests to the same teacher, including declined ones. A family who asked three times and was declined three times is visible for a reason (BR-11).
Never route this through a coordinator. None is required and requiring one would make an everyday conversation into an event (BR-8).

reversal.statement: Cancelling the request before the meeting. It is never deleted — a declined or cancelled request stays on the record (BR-6, BR-11, E9).

parameters.notes: Whether it happened (BR-7). Where nobody attended, that is recorded rather than left blank (A7).

parameters.name: note
parameters.notes: Maximum 1000 characters. What arose, held against the student and visible to the coordinator (BR-7). The teacher's own account of a conversation about a child.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Took place, or Did not take place.

fields.name: note_held_against
fields.description: The student. Visible to the coordinator (BR-7).

fields.name: note_visible_to_guardian
fields.description: Not decided anywhere in this use case.

fields.name: previous_notes
fields.description: Earlier meeting notes about this child. A pattern of concerns about one child is visible to somebody (BR-7).

errors.meaning: The teacher does not teach that child.
errors.note: There is no route to record a note about a child they do not teach.

errors.meaning: The slot has not yet passed.
errors.note: The outcome is recorded after the meeting.

planningRules.rule: Never write the note. It is the teacher's account of a conversation about a child, held against that child and read by the coordinator (BR-7) — a summary a planner produced would be a record of something it did not hear.
Never record a meeting as having taken place unless the actor says so. Where nobody attended, that is what is recorded (A7), and it is what makes a family who arranges and does not come visible.

Report that the note is visible to the coordinator, and that whether the guardian sees it is undecided. A teacher writing about a child should know who reads it, and this use case does not settle the second half.
Report earlier notes about the same child. A pattern of concerns is the reason the note is held against the student rather than against the meeting (BR-7).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: An outcome is not withdrawn. It records what happened at a meeting on a date, and the note stays against the student.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Recorded against the child. Report that the coordinator can see it and that earlier notes about this child exist (PR-4) — and that whether the guardian sees it is not settled anywhere (PR-3).

steps.note: The outcome is recorded; the note is left empty rather than composed (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Recorded as having taken place, with no note. Report that the note is optional but is the teacher's own account — it is held against the child and read by the coordinator later, so a summary written by anything other than the person in the room would be a record of a conversation it did not hear.

steps.note: Recorded as not having taken place rather than left blank (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Recorded. Report that a meeting nobody attended is worth recording rather than leaving — it is what makes a family who arranges a meeting and does not come visible to the coordinator, and an unrecorded one simply disappears.
